defmodule Rocola.Spotify do
  @moduledoc """
  The only way the rest of the app talks to Spotify. Callers use these functions;
  they delegate to the adapter set in `config :rocola, :spotify`
  (`Rocola.Spotify.Fake` by default, `Rocola.Spotify.Web` later).

  A new capability = a new callback here + `Fake` implementation + `Web` stub.
  """

  @type track :: %{
          uri: String.t(),
          name: String.t(),
          artist: String.t(),
          duration_ms: pos_integer()
        }
  @type device :: %{
          id: String.t(),
          name: String.t(),
          is_active: boolean(),
          is_restricted: boolean()
        }

  @callback search(query :: String.t()) :: {:ok, [track]} | {:error, term}
  @callback devices() :: {:ok, [device]} | {:error, term}
  @callback transfer_playback(device_id :: String.t()) :: :ok | {:error, term}
  # Add-only: Spotify's API can append to the queue but never remove or reorder.
  @callback add_to_queue(uri :: String.t()) :: :ok | {:error, term}
  @callback queue() :: {:ok, [track]} | {:error, term}
  @callback now_playing() :: {:ok, track | nil} | {:error, term}

  defp adapter, do: Application.fetch_env!(:rocola, :spotify)

  def search(q), do: adapter().search(q)
  def devices, do: adapter().devices()
  def transfer_playback(id), do: adapter().transfer_playback(id)
  def add_to_queue(uri), do: adapter().add_to_queue(uri)
  def queue, do: adapter().queue()
  def now_playing, do: adapter().now_playing()
end

    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  scope "/", RocolaWeb do
    pipe_through :browser

    get "/", PageController, :home
  end

  # Other scopes may use custom stacks.
  # scope "/api", RocolaWeb do

  # end

  # Enable LiveDashboard in development

    # If you want to use the LiveDashboard in production, you should put
    # it behind authentication and allow only admins to access it.

      pipe_through :browser

      live_dashboard "/dashboard", metrics: RocolaWeb.Telemetry
    end
  end
end

# 001: Architecture

## Decisions
- **Spotify behind a behaviour.** `Rocola.Spotify` defines the callbacks; `Fake` (default in dev/test)
  and `Web` (real API + `TokenServer`, stub) implement them. Switching is config plus credentials.
  Why: build and test with no account, token or network.
- **Own queue.** Spotify's API can add to its queue but not remove or reorder, so Rocola keeps its
  queue in SQLite (skips, votes, per-guest limits) and feeds Spotify one song ahead.
- **Fake mirrors real limits** (add-only queue, restricted devices, active device required) so
  behaviour proven against it carries over to the real adapter.
- **Stack:** Phoenix LiveView, SQLite (`ecto_sqlite3`), `mix release` for aarch64 on a Raspberry Pi.
- **Tidewave** (dev only) gives the coding agent access to the running app over MCP.

defmodule RocolaWeb.AdminLiveTest do
  use RocolaWeb.ConnCase
  import Phoenix.LiveViewTest

  setup do
    Rocola.Spotify.Fake.reset()
    :ok
  end

  test "lists devices; restricted one is unavailable and unselectable", %{conn: conn} do
    {:ok, lv, html} = live(conn, ~p"/admin")
    assert html =~ "Living Room"
    assert html =~ "(unavailable)"
    assert has_element?(lv, "#device-fake-locked button[disabled]")
    refute has_element?(lv, "#device-fake-living-room button[disabled]")

    # forged event must not reach Spotify
    render_click(lv, "select", %{"id" => "fake-locked"})
    assert {:ok, devs} = Rocola.Spotify.devices()
    refute Enum.any?(devs, & &1.is_active)
  end

  test "select activates a device; refresh works", %{conn: conn} do
    {:ok, lv, _} = live(conn, ~p"/admin")
    lv |> element("#device-fake-living-room button") |> render_click()
    assert render(lv) =~ "(active)"
    assert lv |> element("#refresh") |> render_click() =~ "Living Room"
  end
end

defmodule RocolaWeb.Router do
  use RocolaWeb, :router

  pipeline :browser do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_live_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {RocolaWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :protect_from_forgery
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
  end

  pipeline :api do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  scope "/", RocolaWeb do
    pipe_through :browser

    get "/", PageController, :home
  end

  # Other scopes may use custom stacks.
  # scope "/api", RocolaWeb do
  #   pipe_through :api
  # end

  # Enable LiveDashboard in development
  if Application.compile_env(:rocola, :dev_routes) do
    # If you want to use the LiveDashboard in production, you should put
    # it behind authentication and allow only admins to access it.
    # If your application does not have an admins-only section yet,
    # you can use Plug.BasicAuth to set up some basic authentication
    # as long as you are also using SSL (which you should anyway).
    import Phoenix.LiveDashboard.Router

    scope "/dev" do
      pipe_through :browser

      live_dashboard "/dashboard", metrics: RocolaWeb.Telemetry
    end
  end
end

`/admin` now lists playback devices with a Refresh button, and `mix precommit` passes (11 tests, 0 failures). The first run logged a transient "database is locked" error, and the rerun was clean. Nothing is committed.

- **Restricted devices:** they show "(unavailable)" and their Select button is disabled. The `select` handler also looks the device up in the loaded list and refuses restricted ones, so a forged event never reaches Spotify.
- **What Select does:** it switches playback to that device with `Rocola.Spotify.transfer_playback`, and the active device is marked "(active)".
- **Changes:**
  - New `lib/rocola_web/live/admin_live.ex`.
  - A `live "/admin"` route in `router.ex`.
  - Tests in `test/rocola_web/live/admin_live_test.exs` covering the disabled button, the forged event, select, and refresh.
- **Design choice:** there is no `Rocola.Jukebox` context yet, so the LiveView calls the `Rocola.Spotify` behaviour directly. It never calls an adapter or the Repo.
- **Skipped:** auth on `/admin` and live polling. Add auth before exposing the page beyond your home network.

The three deleted `.claude/skills/session-steps/*` files were already deleted in your working tree before I started. I left them alone.
